## Deviations and judgement calls (for Opus)

1. **D1 - ordering.** The first script files were written before the GR-7 receipt and before the requirement ledger
   (`execute/01-start.md` steps 5 and 7). Both were recorded afterwards (`research-exec/r1-gr7-exec-923.md`, `r1-01-ledger.md`),
   before any further write. GR-7: Omah has no modal page in the library (UNVERIFIED, not relied on).
2. **D2 - registry key `widths`** (`{ min?, max? }`, inclusive viewport widths) added beyond the R1 key list. Evidence: 98 triggers
   exist only below 640 (the admin hamburger) and 84 only above it (the locale dropdown, row-click dialogs); without it those states
   cannot be registered, because the gate fails an `open` selector that matches nothing. Validator + tests cover it.
3. **D3 - discovery (b).** The literal rule lists 26 Stories (the empty / error / loading Stories of six chart Stories and the
   `DialogFooter` / `DialogSections` pattern Stories) whose files import an overlay component but render no trigger. They cannot
   be given a row (a row must open a portal). `--discover` therefore clicks every candidate trigger of a flagged Story at 390 and
   1440 and lists it as a miss only if one opens an unregistered portal; the literal list is still printed with the click-through
   result. Run result: 26 listed, 0 misses.
4. **D4 - responsive presentation.** The registry declares the wide presentation. Below 640 a Select / Combobox / Menu / Modal is the
   canonical bottom sheet (Mantine Drawer): a modal presentation (Modal / Drawer / `aria-modal`) is measured as `trap` whatever the
   state declared; `close-control` is not applicable on a sheet that renders none; `outside` is not applicable when the overlay covers
   every corner; focus return is checked only when the trigger can hold focus (a clicked table cell cannot); the actions of the app
   root are not measured while a modal is open (the app is inert).
5. **D5 - metric definitions made precise** after sampling the build for false positives: `component-overflow` = a content element
   (text, control or media) past its parent's padding box, excluding table cells, a side with a negative margin (full-bleed), and an
   element wholly outside its clipping ancestor (a carousel slide); `text-hidden` requires text actually outside the element's
   padding box (not a taller inner box); `viewport-overflow` excludes a closed off-canvas panel (transformed, wholly outside) and
   content hidden by an `overflow:hidden` ancestor; `action-hidden` counts the page scroll as reachability; a dialog under another
   dialog is not "covered". There is no baseline, allowlist or suppression.
6. **D6 - selectors** are structural paths from `#storybook-root` (`:scope > ...`), joined with `, ` across the width classes and
   resolved to the visible match; they depend on the Story DOM. When a Story changes, `open-failed` shows it.
7. **D7 - runtime.** The full run takes 4 021 s on 20 logical CPUs with 10 workers - above a typical PR CI budget. Levers that keep
   the contract: `--jobs`, `--stories` / `--widths` / `--locales` for task runs; Opus decides how the CI step is scoped (kickoff §9).
8. **D8 - closed sweep** measures only the unregistered-portal rule (R3 wording), not the other metrics.
9. `scripts/` is ESLint-ignored, so `npm run lint` does not cover the new files; the test file is covered by `typecheck`.
10. **Concurrent changes outside this task.** `.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/rules/*` changed during the session (`r1-00-status-before.txt` vs
    `r1-61-status-after.txt`); none was edited by this session.
11. The Task 859 Revision 15 execution that was opened in the same session before this task was left untouched (no source write);
    859 starts after 923 (backlog).

## Deviations and judgement calls (for Opus)

1. **D9 - discovery (b).** R14 asks for (b) = 0, but 26 Stories (chart empty/error/loading Stories, `DialogFooter`, `DialogSections`) import an overlay component and render no trigger, so no row can exist (a row must open a portal). (b) is therefore "imports an overlay, no row, and one of its triggers opens a portal" = 0; the 26 are printed as informational with the proof that every candidate was clicked. Same reasoning as the first pass D3, now with an uncapped click-through of every Story.
2. **D10 - `widths` overrides.** 19 states were not one clean theme-grid run in the probe; decided from the sequential bisect (`r2-32-widths-analyse.mjs` `OVERRIDES`): `all-photos` x6 -> `max: 767` (the coarse probe was noisy), `public-visibility`/`unassigned` x11 -> `max: 639`, `relativetime` -> `min: 640`, `usermenu` -> no `widths`. Five new wide variants that open from 641 (`rangedatepicker` x2, `userpickerfieldview` x3) -> `min: 640`. All register the contract range so the gate shows the 640/641 disagreement.
3. **D11 - bounds are stricter than R11 spelled out.** "Clipped away" (carousel) needs a scroll region or a transformed track; the "stacked dialog" cover needs a different portal root. ## Deviations and judgement calls (for Opus)

1. **D16 - R15 read literally flags four classes of positioned content that are working UI.** Carousel / gallery tracks (`div` "transformed" past `div.h-full` / `div._fill_…` in `listingdetailpattern`, `listingdetailview`, `lightboxview`, `listinggallerypattern`: 288 + 144 + 36 + 36 detail lines in the full run), the image layer of listing cards (`img._imageLayer_` absolute+transformed past `div._frame_…`: `listingcardtrack` 140, `homepagelistinggrids` 40, `listingcardpattern` 36, `listingcard` 32, `favoritesshell` 20), Leaflet map internals (`div.leaflet-popup`, `a.leaflet-popup-close-button` past `div.listing-map`: 114 + 114), and chart internals (`admindashboardview` svg / `div.m_…` past `div.m_e…`: 80, `dashboardsemidonut` 8). Whether these are defects or by-design clipped content is a product / owner question; **I added no exemption** (the same defect class as review 2 finding 1: an exemption without a bound and a fixture pair). If Opus wants a bounded exemption (e.g. a transformed track inside a clipping ancestor, as `clippedAway` already does for the in-flow path), it needs a bound, a planted + benign fixture pair and a mutation proof; they are listed under "new - Opus to file" in the meantime. Classification of a whole-registry sample on the pre-R16 build: `r3-sample-r15-classes.txt`.
2. **D17 - the Revision 1 fixture `stacked-dialogs`.** R15 correctly flagged it: its first dialog had no height and the absolutely positioned Delete button hung ~40 px below the box. Its benign intent (Delete lies under the confirmation dialog of a second portal root) is kept; the first dialog got `height:200px` (`r3-20-gen-fixtures.mjs` patches it). The self-test still passes `stacked-dialogs` / `covered-action` as before.
3. **D18 - retry design.** The retry runs the whole job again on a fresh page; measured violations of the first attempt are carried into the retried result so a retry can only add a recovery, never clear a finding; every row of a retried job carries `retry` (not only the failing one); `open-never` carries `retry` too (its second failure is the violation).
4. **D19 - the retry did not recover anything in the full run**: the 24 retried jobs are the deterministic 640 cells (924). The Revision 1 flake at 639 did not recur, so the retry's recovery path is proved only by the self-test fixture `open-flaky-once` and the unit tests.
5. **D20 - R17 counts.** "found" = clicked + not operable; a candidate not attempted after a reload failure counts as not operable with that reason. The non-operable list is informational (it lists real Stories whose control cannot be clicked within 2.5 s, e.g. `richtexteditor`, `savesearchbutton`, `userpickerfieldview`); I did not triage it.
6. **D21 - the full run needs a rebuilt Storybook** (`r3-80-build-storybook.txt` precedes discover and the full run; the earlier sample run was on the old build and is kept only as `r3-sample-r15-*`).
7. The Bash tool hook blocks running a saved shell script, so the chains were run as inline commands. The security-guidance hook warned about `innerHTML` in the generated fixtures (static constants). Nothing was bypassed.

## Deviations and judgement calls (for Opus)

1. **D26 - the `track-active-slide-inside` PASS case asserts `component-overflow` only on `portal:0`** (new optional case key `greenRules` in `verify.mjs`: root -> rules that must be empty; the other rules of that root are printed as "observed, not asserted"). The off-screen slide `button`s (`aria-hidden`, `tabindex="-1"`, clipped away by the `overflow: hidden` frame) still trigger the *action* rules: `action-covered` on `portal:0` of the fixture, and `action-hidden` in the real app root (288 details in `listingdetailpattern` app rows of `r4-full`, previously masked while the track was a failure). An all-rules-green PASS is impossible with a literal `overflow: hidden` frame and button slides. Option for Opus: a bounded exemption in the action rules for a control that is clipped away, hidden from AT and out of the tab order. I did not add one (outside R22).
2. **D27 - the faithful gallery DOM (in-flow flex slides in a translated track) leaves a residual detail R22 does not cover:** the visible, in-frame slide `button` is flagged by the in-flow path (`button.mantine-focus-auto "" x 16..374 past div -342..16`, the slide measured against its displaced track box). The PASS fixture therefore uses absolutely positioned slides. Gallery Stories will keep failing `component-overflow` after 859 R58 fixes the counter. It is not in the AC21 `gallery-track` count (the script counts positioned details only); `r5-71` prints it "for information" (228 details) and the owner table lists it as its own "new - Opus to file" row.
3. **D28 - the printed detail lists are capped:** a rule's list in one row holds at most 12 details and then a tail `…+N more (T in total)` (`in-page.mjs:410`). With the 144 slide-wrapper details gone, more counters are printed (228 against 156 in Revision 3); the AC21 classes count printed details. 36 `listingdetailpattern--default` rows still carry a tail with 72 unprinted details; their text is not recorded, so "0 of any other kind" covers the printed details only.
4. **D29 - "zero-size boxes are ignored" is read strictly:** width 0 AND height 0.
5. **D30 - whole-suite vitest.** Runs, all on unchanged code (`scripts/` only; no failing file imports `scripts/`): run 1 red (9 tests in `ResetPasswordClient.smoke` + `CabinetPasswordSection.smoke`), **run 2 green (2 573 / 2 573)**, run 3 red (2, `RangeDatePicker.smoke` keyboard flow), run 4 red (25, 9 files), 5 red (23, 9 files), 6 red (23, 9 files), 7 red (26, 9 files), 10 red (28, 11 files), 11 red (26, 9 files). Every failure is `Test timed out in 5000ms` / `15000ms` or the lookup that follows a timed-out render. The suite took 48 s in the green run and 130-142 s in the later ones; no other heavy process of mine was running (checked: `Get-Process`, CPU about 10 %). Diagnostics, not `npm test`: `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=6` twice (`r5-91-vitest-all-8/9-maxworkers6.txt`): 1 failure each, the same `RangeDatePicker.smoke` test (5 000 ms); the failing files alone: `r5-91-vitest-failed-files-isolated.txt` (red, run while analysis scripts were running) and `r5-91-vitest-failed-files-isolated-2.txt` (3 files, 57/57 green). Every red run is kept; none was hidden. Revision 3 saw the same two files fail once (its D24).
6. **D31 - `check:mojibake` exit 1.** `scripts/check-mojibake.mjs:138-141` runs the tracked-plus-untracked file listing (a read-only Git command) through `spawnSync` with the default 1 MiB `maxBuffer`; the listing is now 1 050 626 bytes (`r5-95-probe-enobuf.txt`: `status null`, `ENOBUFS`), so it throws `git ls-files failed:` with an empty stderr. The script is outside the write set and is unchanged. Diagnostic: `r5-95-spawn-maxbuffer-preload.mjs` raises `maxBuffer` for that call only (`node --import … scripts/check-mojibake.mjs`) -> `r5-95-mojibake-maxbuffer.txt` exit 0, "0 artifacts in 11949 files" (Revision 3: 11 859 files); the first preload attempt (named export not re-synced) is kept as `r5-95-mojibake-maxbuffer-attempt1-preload-not-synced.txt`. A task to fix the script's buffer is Opus's to file.
7. **D32 - the chart lines (31 + 39, was 40 + 48) are not an effect of R22.** `r5-72-chart-row-diff.txt`: of the chart-class rows, 39 are present in both runs with identical details (text ignored), 9 are only in `r4-full` (all `admindashboardview`, 1024, the `~en-english` interaction states: 2 `en`, 2 `it`, 2 `uk`, 3 `sq`) and 0 only in `r5-full`; in `r5-full` those nine rows fail other rules (text-clamp / text-ellipsis / text-hidden). The detail they lost is a partial overlap (`x 791.7..1011.7 past 771.7..998.7`), which R22's wholly-out slide path never touches. Three narrowed repeats of the same Story at 1024 (`r5-73-chart-repeat-1/2/3.txt`) show the detail on all 24 rows each time (`~en-english` in all four locales, identical in the three runs). `r5-85-row-diff.txt`: 69 rows of the 22 740 changed their failing-rule set against `r4-full`, over 9 different rules (`focus-trap`, `focus-open`, `dismiss-*`, `target-small`, `action-hidden`, `viewport-overflow`, `component-overflow`), not only `component-overflow` - the same full-run timing sensitivity as the vitest timeouts of D30; I cannot attribute it to R22.
8. The Bash tool's `cd` persists between calls; every command ran from the repository root (absolute paths). The Bash hook rejected one compound command that contained a Git word inside a heredoc; the files were written with the Write tool instead. Nothing was bypassed.

I cannot attribute it to a requirement; I take it for the timing of the ApexCharts draw after a locale switch (same reading as D32).

Several of these files are modified or untracked in the working tree for reasons outside this task; I changed no test, timeout or config.
4. **D36 - the 94 listed row changes against `r5-full`** (`r6-85-row-diff.txt`; the script attributes by detail only): (i) 36 `listingdetailpattern` gallery rows: the base list held 7 in-flow button details + 7 counters and a tail, the new list holds the 7 counters and no tail (14 -> 7 details) - the printed counters rise by 36, an effect of the 12-detail cap (D28), not new counters; (ii) 16 action-rule changes on rows that carry a `retry` key in `r5-full` (their `notApplicable` already says "modal open, app behind it inert", yet the list holds details); the same rows have no retry key and no details in `r6-full`; (iii) 15 chart `component-overflow` changes (9 vanished, 6 appeared) - D34; (iv) 7 `dismiss-close-control` on `listingcontactpattern` failing -> green (the toast close control that "cannot be clicked" in `r5-full`) - consistent with R26 (a), not provable by row; (v) 18 `dismiss-*` changes that go **both** ways across admin Stories (11 failing -> green, 7 green -> failing: "the portal is still visible N ms after the dismissal"); the 1 s dismissal bound is unchanged by R26, so I read this as run-to-run timing of the full run (10 workers) and report it; (vi) 1 `listingcontactpattern` `viewport-overflow` and 1 `authsheet` `component-overflow` detail gone.

## Deviations and judgement calls (for Opus)

1. **D39 - closed sweep and range jobs use the default 8 000 ms bound** (they passed 3 000 / 2 500 ms before) so that there is one settle function and one bound. `discover.mjs` (out of scope) still passes its own 1 500 ms.
2. **D40 - `dismissMs` is measured from just before the dismissal event**, so a close time never undercounts; the 5 000 ms failure bound counts from after the action. `settle` on a row is the settle immediately before the measurement (after the open); a row where no settle ran carries `{ms: 0, bounded: false}`. `verify.mjs` skips its "settle did not hit the bound" check for the cases that expect `portal-count` (a declared-but-never-opening state legitimately waits out the bound). The AC30 / AC31 probe copies differ from the review-6 originals by the comment, the import path (one `../` fewer: the copies live one directory higher) and the usage line.
3. **D41 - the three differing cells were isolated and sampled as AC32 asks.** Isolation: `--stories <story> --widths <w> --locales <l> --no-closed`, 3 runs per cell (`r7-62-iso*`), all three agree with run b. Sampling: `r7-63-differing-cells-probe.mjs` (the whole `runStateJob` at CPU throttle 1x and 4x, 5 trials each; written in the spirit of `rv6-53-chart-settle-probe.mjs`, extended from the chart measure to the whole job) and `r7-64-differing-cells-load-probe.mjs` (the full-run condition: 10 pages in parallel, 3 rounds, 30 jobs per cell).
4. **D42 - `all-photos` sq 390 (Leaflet popup).** `r7-65-leaflet-popup-settle-probe.mjs`: after the settle the popup box is `38..385` (347 px, past the map `37..353`) at throttle 1x and `49..343` (294 px, inside) at 4x; in each case the box is identical 3 000 ms later, the map pane has no animation and does not move. So the width is decided once, when the popup opens, by what the page has loaded at that moment (the cause of the difference is not isolated); a settle can not see it because nothing changes afterwards. In run a the settle took 1 281 ms (619 ms in run b): the machine was busier. The same race explains the Leaflet lines 112 + 1 + 113 of run a against 110 + 4 + 114 of run b. **Question for Opus:** a Leaflet popup that is wider than its map on a fast machine and inside it on a slow one is a product defect (owner row "listingdetailview, Leaflet popup" above) and a gate-determinism gap: should the settle wait for a condition on the popup content (images / fonts loaded) - an extension of R31 that I did not make?
5. **D43 - `activity-error` uk 320 and `share-listing` en 320 occurred once each, in run a only.** Not reproduced: 3 isolated runs, 10 throttled trials and 30 loaded jobs each. In run a the first cell hit the settle bound (8 063 ms) with the portal never opened, so its verdict is a `portal-count` and an unsettled app root; the second is a dismissal where Escape did not close the popover within 5 000 ms while the outside click closed it in 177 ms (a key handler that needs the focus inside the popover? not isolated). Each is one job in about 12 800 state jobs of its run; I take them for load of the machine in run a, which is also the slower run (9 604 s against 8 028 s), but I can not prove that.
6. **D44 - `mantine-primitives-relativetime--default` at 640 hits the 8 000 ms settle bound in both runs** (a text that updates by timer; the layout signature changes forever). The page is measured as it is and the summary lists it; its rows carry `settle.bounded: true`.
7. **D45 - evidence hygiene.** (a) My first early self-test transcript wrapper recorded the wrong exit code; it was re-run with a `code=$?` capture (`r7-30-verify-early.txt`, exit 0) and the final run is `r7-83-verify.txt`. (b) `r7-84-ac32-checks.mjs` first classified the 925 `error-screen` cell by its detail text and printed it as "owned by neither"; it now classifies by the Story (`custom-range-too-long`) and both `r7-84-ac32-checks-{a,b}.txt` were re-run. (c) One writer per evidence file, and no other process ran while a full run or the self-test ran (kickoff 15.5).
8. The repository has many uncommitted and untracked files (a porcelain list of about 1 900 lines, including the whole `scripts/__fixtures__/rendered-state-census/` directory); the owner does all version-control mutations. Nothing was bypassed.

## Database checks for Opus (owner-run, read-only) — requested by the owner 2026-10-17

The owner asked that these be recorded here so that Opus gives the owner the commands to run against the live database. Sonnet cannot verify them: the
Supabase migrations (row-level-security policies and `SECURITY DEFINER` functions) are not in the repository. Sonnet did not write the commands. Each row is a
QUESTION whose answer decides whether a finding is a real hole; until it is answered the application code does not rely on the answer (where the code could be
made independent of the database it was, see "Already hardened in code").

| ID | Object to inspect | Question to answer | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| S40 | function `get_listing_owner_contact(listing_id_param)` (called by `modules/listings/actions/getListingOwnerContact.ts`, a public Server Action) | (1) Does the function body require an authenticated session (`auth.uid() is not null`) or accept anonymous callers? (2) Does it return the phone only for a listing that is publicly viewable (status), or for any id? (3) Is there any rate limit, per caller or per IP, on calls to it? (4) Which roles hold `EXECUTE` on it (`anon`, `authenticated`, `public`)? | A script can walk listing ids and collect every owner's phone number and WhatsApp number. |
| S20 / S27 | row-level-security policies on `collections`, `collection_items`, `listings` (DELETE), `listing_images` | Is there a policy that limits `collection_items` writes to the owner of the collection, and `listings` / `listing_images` deletes to the owner or to staff? | The actions now check ownership themselves; the policy is the second line of defence and should exist. |
| S32 | policy / grants on `users.status`, `users.suspended_until`, `users.block_reason` | Can a signed-in user update their own `status` or `suspended_until`? | A blocked person who can clear their own block bypasses `getBlockedError`. |
| S31 | trigger on `auth.users` (profile creation) and the column `users.company_id` | Does a trigger copy `raw_user_meta_data` fields (`role`, `company_id`, `user_type`, `is_verified`) into `public.users`? Can a user update their own `company_id`, `role`, `is_verified`? | The code ignores `role` / `is_verified` from metadata and now passes only six whitelisted metadata keys, but a database trigger could still read them. |
| S3 / S4 | storage / table policies behind `companies`, `popular_locations` photos | Who may insert or update `companies` rows? | `createCompanyAction` is callable before a session exists. |
| S26 | `contact_inquiries`, `listing_inquiries` | Any unique / rate constraint per `requester_ip`? | The application rate limit trusts `x-forwarded-for`. |
| general | all tables with row-level security | Is RLS enabled on every table in `public`, and which tables have no policy? | The tests prove the application filters by the caller; they cannot prove the database refuses a direct request with the public anon key. |

**Answered on 2026-10-17 by the owner-authorised database verification (see "Database verification with two user sessions" below):**

- **S40** — the function requires a session (`auth.uid()` is checked, anonymous is refused) and returns the owner phone / WhatsApp of every public listing to ANY registered account; pending listings return nothing; no rate limit. Quota decision = D-quota.
- **S32** — YES, a signed-in user can update their own `status`, `block_reason`, `suspended_until` (and `role`, `is_verified`, `deleted_at`, `public_id`) through the REST API: finding S60 / S59, proven.
- **S31** — the only trigger on `auth.users` is `handle_new_user`; it copies `role` from the sign-up metadata (S66, proven) and `user_type`; `is_verified` is forced false. A user can also update their own `role` (S59).
- **S20 / S27, S3 / S4, S26** — NOT examined by this run (collections / images policies were only checked for cross-user writes on favourites and images: refused; `companies` and `popular_locations` write policies, and per-IP constraints on inquiries, remain open questions).
- **general** — every one of the 50 tables in `public` has RLS enabled; tables with no policy for a role also have no grant for it (reads answer 42501).

### Contact-protection requirements (owner, 2026-10-17) — recorded for Opus, NOT implemented

Source: two owner messages of 2026-10-17 pasted into the chat, plus one correction. They are task-design and policy input; policy, hooks and CI are Opus' (the owner's text says so), and Sonnet's product work is blocked until a contract exists (see the next section).

**Scope.** Every way to reach the listing owner: (1) Call, (2) WhatsApp, (3) Write a message including the Send button of the form. A future Chat button is planned, not built.
**Policy for all of them.** Cloudflare Turnstile **Invisible** (no checkbox, no manual step), mandatory server-side validation, all users and all roles without exception, no bypass through a direct Server Action call, a direct RPC or the database, server limits on rate and parallelism that are atomic in a shared store and independent of role, **no hard daily quota**.
**Call / WhatsApp.** The tap starts a silent check; the server verifies the token, the user and the right to receive the contact; only then is the contact returned and the action started. `get_listing_owner_contact` called directly must not allow a bypass.
**Message.** The tap starts a silent check, then the form opens; **Send** needs a fresh server-side confirmation of its own (opening the form does not replace it); `submitListingInquiry` must not create an inquiry, send an e-mail or create a notification without it; a direct Server Action call also needs it; check and close direct INSERT into `listing_inquiries` and other RPCs. The confirmation is bound to the operation, the listing and the verified user session; the e-mail typed in the form is not proof of identity; a contact-open token must not work for sending and a form-open token must not allow unlimited sending. A long form gets a fresh confirmation in the background; on a check error the typed text is kept and a retry is possible; a resend after a network failure must not duplicate the inquiry, e-mail or notification.
**Rate limits.** Review `submitListingInquiry`: it limits 5 inquiries per IP per hour and skips the limit for an unknown IP. A shared IP must not be the only reason to block and a missing IP must not switch protection off.
**Acceptance.** All three buttons, the real sending, all roles, tokens reused, parallel requests, direct calls.
**Correction on guests (owner, same day).** "У гостя не має бути доступу до картки контактів власника оголошення" — the earlier sentence about guests who may send messages was a slip; the whole card (Call, WhatsApp, Message) is for signed-in people only. Verified in source: the UI already shows a guest only the sign-in call to action (`guestCta`), `ListingMobileCTA` renders nothing for a guest, and the database refuses anonymous callers of `get_listing_owner_contact`. What still lets a guest in: `submitListingInquiry` and `trackListingContactEvent` do not require a session (a guest can call the Server Actions directly), and comments in `page.tsx`, `contactEvents.ts`, `submitListingInquiry.ts`, `ListingContact.tsx` describe guest paths as allowed. The comments are in the scope of the D8/D9 record (comment-only); the behaviour belongs to the contact-protection task.

**Future Chat (owner, same day) — to be saved in the planning record and in the workflow gates by Opus.** Not built now. Any later task that adds, changes or activates the Chat button, conversation creation, message sending or the matching Server Action / HTTP endpoint / RPC / Realtime path must carry an explicit anti-automation and access-control contract; without it the task must not pass preparation. A call to a Turnstile helper is not enough: the result must decide whether the protected operation runs. Contract content: real components and server entry points; the check on the Chat tap; server checks on conversation creation and on sending; binding to session, resource and operation; separate authorisation of conversations and messages (a successful Turnstile grants no right to read other people's conversations); all roles; forbidden side effects on refusal; frontend/server allow, deny and error cases; applicable database, HTTP, browser, provider and Realtime checks. The contract is kept separate from the contact-protection contract; chat tests stay `planned` (no fake chat, no skipped/TODO in a passed report, never marked implemented or reviewed before a real implementation); a chat product diff cannot pass as planned or as documentation Q0; activation is blocked until the allowed scenario, per-role refusal, forged / expired / replayed tokens, no transfer between users and resources, direct calls and parallel requests, no forbidden e-mails / notifications / messages on refusal, recovery without loss or duplicates, independent review and fresh results are shown. The workflow gate itself must be proven by checks: a correct future plan is accepted, an implementation task without the contract is rejected, a product diff with a planned contract is rejected, missing / skipped / failed required checks never give a positive result.

#### Evidence collected for the contact-protection design (read-only, synthetic data, cleaned up)

- **Entry points.** Call / WhatsApp: `ListingContact.tsx` (`handleContactClick`) and `ListingMobileCTA.tsx` (`handleCallClick`, `handleWhatsAppClick`), both through the Server Action `getListingOwnerContact` -> `get_listing_owner_contact`. Message: `ListingInquiryDialog.tsx` -> Server Action `submitListingInquiry`. `components/listing/WhatsAppContactButton.tsx` takes the raw phone as props and has **no consumer** (dead code that would bypass everything if used). `trackListingContactEvent` records only WhatsApp taps and needs no session.
- **`submitListingInquiry` today.** No human check and no session requirement; IP limit 5 per hour read from `x-forwarded-for` / `x-real-ip`; an unknown IP is not limited and is stored as null; the count is a read followed by an insert (not atomic, parallel requests pass); no idempotency (after `email_transient` the row already exists and the dialog treats it as success, but any retry after another failure creates a second row, e-mail and notification); the owner e-mail and a bell notification are created after the row; the typed e-mail is only used for `replyTo`.
- **Direct paths (probe `contact-bypass-probe.cjs`, 14 probes, 3 open):** `D04` an **administrator** can INSERT into `listing_inquiries` directly (anonymous, a normal user and a moderator are refused by RLS) — through finding S59 any user can become administrator first; `D10` any signed-in account and `D11` an administrator receive the owner phone from `get_listing_owner_contact` with their own token, with no Server Action and no check. Closed: INSERT into `listing_contact_events` and `notifications`, `process_saved_search_notify`, reading the phone from `users` or from the public listing row.
- **Cloudflare Turnstile facts (read 2026-10-17 from developers.cloudflare.com).** A token is valid 300 seconds and can be validated once; a replay answers `timeout-or-duplicate`. `siteverify` takes `secret`, `response`, optional `remoteip` and `idempotency_key` (a UUID so validation can be retried safely) and returns `success`, `challenge_ts`, `hostname`, `error-codes`, `action`, `cdata` (and Enterprise-only `metadata`). The widget parameter `action` is at most 32 characters of letters, digits, `_`, `-`; `cData` is at most 255 of the same; both come back from validation, so the server can bind a token to an operation and to a listing / session value and compare them. Modes: Managed, Non-Interactive, **Invisible** ("Runs challenges completely in the background with no visible widget or loading indicators"); using Invisible requires referencing Cloudflare's Turnstile Privacy Addendum in the site's privacy policy. **Not established from the documentation read:** where the mode is chosen (dashboard widget vs client code) and whether separate widgets per operation are advised; the existing `CaptchaWidget` component and `verifyTurnstile` serve the sign-up forms.
- **Consequence for design (for Opus to decide, not decided here).** The database function cannot verify a Turnstile token itself, so "direct `get_listing_owner_contact` must not bypass" means the function is callable only by the server (`service_role`) and the Server Action passes the verified user; the quota / rate state lives in the database (atomic) and the same applies to inquiries (service-role only INSERT, administrators included). This also requires the S59 fix, otherwise a user can promote themselves around any of it.

### Local environment warning (2026-10-17)

`.env.local` contains `CLOUDINARY_DELETE_MODE=enabled`. Before fix S48 the Cloudinary clean-up never found an asset (the id kept its `.jpg`), so replacing an avatar or deleting a listing
deleted nothing. After S48 the clean-up works: on a machine with this setting, replacing an avatar, editing a listing's images or deleting a listing now really destroys the replaced
files in the Cloudinary cloud (an asset any table still points to is skipped by the reference check). Unit tests never reach Cloudinary (it is mocked). If this is not wanted on a
development machine, set the value to anything other than `enabled`. Until the owner authorised the database check below, Sonnet did not read or use the Supabase keys of `.env.local`; only variable NAMES and this one value were listed.

The condition is applied exactly as R58 (a) states; the file's header (v5, item 5) and the INFO check `H01e` record it. Whether the condition should admit `service_role` is Opus's decision. ### 3. Facts, blocked parts and judgement calls for Opus

1. **R64 (a) currency conversion — BLOCKED.** The kickoff converts the starting price "at the rate the site uses at that moment" and says to report `BLOCKED` if the database cannot convert. FACT (`r16-00-capture.txt`): `public.currency_rates` holds ONE row, EUR -> ALL 108.50, fetched 2026-04-18; `listing_currency` has two labels (ALL, EUR); `rg "currency_rates" src` finds no reader or writer (the table appears only in `docs/` and in Task 870's privilege scripts); the live rate is read from iliria98.com every hour and never stored (`src/lib/getExchangeRateServer.ts`, C680, C681). INFERENCE: the database has no rate it could convert at. The draft therefore carries a FAIL-SAFE that the kickoff does not state: on a currency change the new price becomes the new starting price and `price_old` is null, so a price in one currency is never compared with a starting price in another (`r16-02b` P10, P11; `r16-03` V718). Opus decides: this fail-safe, a stored rate (the table of R79 (b); `currency_rates` fits structurally, `from_currency`, `to_currency`, `rate`, `fetched_at`, unique `(from, to)`), or a conversion in the server code.
2. **R65 (b) — `generateSlug` does NOT only produce slugs of the new INSERT rule.** FACT (`r16-06-slug-probe.txt`, the real function text run on 15 realistic titles and 20 000 seeded random ones): `"Shitet apartament - 2+1"` gives `shitet-apartament---21-<time>` (two hyphens in a row), `"Zyrë me qira - qendër"` and `"A - B"` the same, a title with no Latin letter or digit (Ukrainian) or only spaces gives `-<time>` (a leading hyphen); 6 of the 15 sample titles are refused (four realistic ones: `"Shitet apartament - 2+1"`, `"A - B"`, `"Zyrë me qira - qendër"` and the Ukrainian title; two degenerate ones: `"   "` and `"---"`), and 57% of the random sample. With the rule as the kickoff states it, `createListing` fails with 42501 for any title that has a hyphen next to a space or no Latin character. The rule in the file is the kickoff's, unchanged; the conflict is recorded in the file's "NOT BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL" item 8 and `r16-03` V707 (INFO, not asserted). Opus decides: fix `generateSlug` (collapse hyphens, a fixed word for an empty base) before the file is applied, or relax the rule.
3. **R63 (a) — public listing numbers skip.** The column default of `public_id` takes one sequence value and the guard's `nextval` the next one, so two consecutive listings differ by 2 (`r16-02b` G1b). The kickoff says "set from `nextval` whatever was supplied"; a variant without the gap (compare with `currval`) exists. Recorded in the file's item 6; Opus's choice.
4. **R62 (a): "trimmed name and last name".** Read as each part trimmed and joined by one space (`"Tina   Padded"` was the first reading's result for padded parts, `r16-02` A2 failed once before the fix); both readings agree on unpadded names.
5. **R62 (c) depends on the order in which the database fires the referential actions** for the three keys to `auth.users` (`contact_inquiries.handled_by`, `contact_inquiry_replies.replied_by`, `email_templates.updated_by`). FACT (`r16-00-capture.txt`): on `auth.users` the cascade to `public.users` (`users_id_fkey`) fires 9th and those three keys 10th, 14th and 15th (same-event triggers fire in name order, `RI_ConstraintTrigger_a_<oid>`; the two re-created keys get larger OIDs); so each of them sees the profile row already gone. Temporary tables with the opposite order keep a null name (`r16-02` R3, INFO), and deleting only a profile row while the Auth row exists nulls the name too (R4, INFO; `deleteAccount` deletes the Auth user). `DX03d` checks one such key on the real table after the apply.
6. FACT: the `pages` column `updated_by` (a staff user id) stays readable by `anon` under R62 (b) as it is today (the captured column list includes it); the kickoff names only `updated_by_name`. Reported, not changed. FACT: no application reader of `pages` or `site_footer` through an anon or session client uses `select('*')` (`rg "from\\(['\"](pages|site_footer)['\"]\\)" src`: the public page reads `content` and `id, title, slug, content, is_published`, the admin page reads explicit columns, the footer reads use the service-role client, C485); UNKNOWN for a reader outside `src/`.
7. **R64 (b), (c) — outside the contract scope.** `src/modules/listings/domain/priceOld.ts` and `priceOld.test.ts`, the tests that pin today's rule (`__tests__/createListing.smoke.test.ts`, `updateListing.smoke.test.ts`, `listingDomain.test.ts`, `listingImages.security.test.ts`) and the display tests are not in the `scope` of `Sprint_78_Task_923_security_record_D8_D9.security.json` (240 paths, listed by `cli.mjs`); `src/**` is a product path, so the hook refuses those writes (`outside its scope ... Opus amends the contract`). R64 (b) is `BLOCKED — contract scope` until Opus adds them. `updateListing.ts` and `createListing.ts` are in scope but cannot change alone: the out-of-scope smoke tests assert today's `price_old` behaviour. The contract has no `SEC-` case for R64.
8. **Wording gap in R69 and R73 (a).** They say the v7 SQL is "written and run only after the owner approves its SHA", while R63–R65 and AC63 ask the executor to write v7 and report its SHA for that approval. Read as: the file may be drafted, applying it waits. The SQL of R69, R73 (a), R75 (c), (f), R77 (e), R78 (a), (b) and R79 (b) is NOT in this v7 draft (section 31, "Waiting for the owner's SQL approval"); the SHA Opus reviews is therefore of a v7 that is not complete, and a later change to the file changes the SHA. Opus decides whether those changes go into this file before the review or into a later file.
9. **Harness slugs.** A session INSERT now needs a plain slug, so the harness's own session-made slugs (`P02`, the per-state `b` check, `V70x`) use `zzsynth<run>-…` without underscores; the clean-up finds both prefixes. Not a product change.
10. UNVERIFIED until an apply: the post-apply branches of `H01`, `DX`, `V` checks; the real `auth.users` cascade ordering for the re-created keys; the `currencies` triggers (not captured; `set_default_currency` writes only changed rows). The harness checks `V740`–`V744` run on a privileged connection inside a transaction that is always rolled back.

The owner's report (translated): "1. I opened the edit page, entered 20 000 000 000 ALL, all fine; entered 20 000 000 000 EUR, it showed the error, all fine. Then I saved
the changes, I was sent to a page saying my listing is under review, then I clicked somewhere and got a 404 error. What is this unstable behaviour? 2. Signed in as the
owner, open the owner's own archived listing: it opens. http://localhost:3000/uk/listings/35-mviht7po: the UX is total crap, I am signed in and I am offered to sign in
again? It simply signs me out of my account, and then I want to sign in but cannot, because it shows an authorization error." Screenshot: the restricted page of
35-mviht7po with the guest header ("Sign in", "Register") and the action "Sign in".

- AC101: confirmed by the owner on the local site (ALL saves, EUR shows the price error). AC103, the owner's path: the owner reports that the own archived listing opens.
- **F16 (confirmed; the code of Task 334, exposed by D53).** `getPostSaveRedirect` (`src/modules/listings/domain/listingSemanticHelpers.ts:101-104`) returns
  `/${locale}/cabinet/listings` for every non-visible status, and `ListingFormShell.tsx:249` (`not_found`) pushes the same path; `ListingFormShell.tsx:259` runs it 3 s after
  the success screen, with no click. No such route exists: `src/app/[locale]/cabinet/` holds `page.tsx` and `statistics/` only, and Git has no history of a
  `cabinet/listings` page. Since D53 every owner edit of an active listing becomes `pending`, so every such save ends on a 404. The existing landing is
  `/{locale}/cabinet?tab=listings` (`src/components/layout/UserMenu.tsx:31`, `MobileNavDrawer.tsx:89`, `src/modules/cabinet/statistics/hrefs.ts:4`). Two tests pin the wrong
  target: `src/modules/listings/domain/__tests__/listingDomain.test.ts:207`, `src/modules/listings/components/__tests__/ListingFormShell.moderation.security.test.tsx:77`.
  Probe `review-35/rv35-01-session-probe.txt`: `/uk/cabinet/listings -> 404`.
- **F17 (confirmed by code; task design of R44/R45): two sources of sign-in truth.** The locale layout (`src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:43`) and the login page
  (`src/app/[locale]/auth/login/page.tsx`, `if (user) redirect(...)`) use `resolveSession()` (an Auth session plus a profile row). `/api/auth/me` (`src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts`,
  Task 923 diff) and the listing page use `requireViewer()`, which also refuses a lookup failure, a non-active status and a deleted profile. For a session that Auth accepts and
  `requireViewer()` refuses, the client header switches to the guest state after its sync, the restricted page offers "Sign in", and the login page sends the person straight
  back: there is no way out. For an account banned in Auth, the middleware ends the session (`src/lib/auth/middleware.ts`, `user_banned`) and the password sign-in shows
  "Invalid email or password" (`AuthSheet.tsx:40` maps "user is banned" to `error_invalid_credentials`). Either path matches the owner's report.

  cabinet again, 35-mviht7po and the catalogue (`/api/auth/me` names a user, the header has no "Sign in", no auth cookie cleared). Its second pass did not change the
  session (the cookie is split into `.0`/`.1` parts, which the probe does not rewrite), so the token-refresh path is not proven.
- **The trigger on the owner's account: UNVERIFIED.** A read-only check of that account's Auth and profile state through the service role was refused by the agent
  permission classifier; it was not attempted another way.
- Not committed by the owner yet: Review 34 (above) is still in the working tree and goes with this record.

error text, and the `npm run dev` terminal output from that moment, or the owner's permission for the read-only account-state check. The D8_D9 contract stays `draft`.

2. **FINDING — R113 (e) as written hides the challenge in the dialog; fixed in the code, to be confirmed by Opus.** §57.2 puts `getToken()` first inside the existing `startTransition(async …)`. `getToken()` calls the widget's `execute()`, and `@marsidev/react-turnstile` 1.5.2 shows the compact challenge by a state update inside `execute()` (`dist/index.js`: the container starts as `width:0;height:0;overflow:hidden` and `execute()` calls `L(h.compact)`, which gives it its 140 px). Inside an async transition that update is held until the transition ends. Measured on the running site (`r33-61`, and the first dialog trial of `r33-60`, which timed out after 60 s): with the literal route the dialog's container stayed `width:100%;height:0px;overflow:hidden` while Cloudflare's 150 x 140 iframe lay clipped under it, so a person who has to tick the box cannot see it and the send ends with the refusal toast after 30 s. The contact card is not affected: its press handler is no transition. Fix in `ListingInquiryDialog.handleSubmit`: the token is requested in the click handler (`const tokenRequest = check?.getToken()`) and **awaited first inside the transition**; the order, the rejection toast, the kept dialog and values, the reset and the `submitListingInquiry` call are exactly as §57.2 (e) states. After pressing WhatsApp, the WhatsApp app does not always open on the phone, and on desktop a WhatsApp tab does not always open so that the desktop app can be opened.` The owner's DevTools Network screenshot of a WhatsApp press shows Cloudflare's challenge requests, then the gateway's Server Action request (initiator `contactGateway.ts:30`) with status 200 after 2.51 s, and no wa.me tab.

- **F22 (P1): WhatsApp and Call open after the click's activation has expired.**
  - `ListingContact.tsx:154-166` awaits the token and the gateway, and only then calls `window.open` (WhatsApp) or clicks a `tel:` link (Call).
  - A browser lets a script open a window only while the click's transient activation lasts, and that activation expires after a timeout (MDN, Glossary "Transient activation" and "User activation").
  - `rv37-31-activation-probe.txt` (Chromium 148) measures that the activation is still active 4.5 s after the click and gone 5.5 s after it. Headless Playwright does not block pop-ups, so that probe reads `navigator.userActivation.isActive`. In the owner's Chrome, a `window.open` without activation is blocked.
  - Before R113 only one database call stood between the click and the opening. Now the human check (seconds) and the gateway (2.51 s on the dev server) stand there, so the time often passes the limit. That is why it fails "not always". Opus's Revision 33 did not consider this.
- **F23 (P2): a failed check waits 30 s in silence.**
  - `getToken()` returns the wrapper's `getResponsePromise()`, which waits for a token for up to 30 s by default (`@marsidev/react-turnstile` 1.5.2, `getResponsePromise(e=3e4,t=100)`).
  - The on-demand widget's `onError` only hides the box (`CaptchaWidget.tsx:108`), so a Cloudflare error is not seen until that timeout.
  - Why no token came for the owner's press of Call is not established. The Turnstile error code in the browser console is needed.
- **Route.** R115 and R116 stay correct and independent of F22 and F23, so Revision 34 stays `ready` as committed and Sonnet executes it now. The correction of F22 and F23 is the next revision (Revision 35; R78 (c) moves after it). It needs the owner's decision on how the number opens after the check (D75) and the console's Turnstile error code for the press of Call.

Status: NEEDS REVISION (Revision 34 ready; F22 and F23 wait for D75 and the console's error code)

### 9. Owner decisions D75 and D76 (Opus, 2026-10-23); the plan of Revision 35

- **D75 (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** `Let's do it differently: replace the "Call" button with a "Show number" button, so that a click on "Show number" lets the user see the phone number. A click on the WhatsApp button opens the WhatsApp app with the chat in the WhatsApp app.`
- **D76 (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** `But these buttons must be protected from bots.`

**Plan of Revision 35.** It is designed against the code after Revision 34 (R116), so it is published once Revision 34 is reviewed. Its claim rows and exact routes are written then.
- **Show number (D75, F22 for Call).** The Call button becomes "Show number" in sq, en, uk and it.
  - A press runs the human check and the gateway, as now (D76).
  - On success the button shows the returned number in place, as a `tel:` link: a later tap dials on a phone; on a desktop the number can be read.
  - Nothing opens after the wait, so the browser's activation limit no longer applies.
  - The number is never in the page before the gateway answers.
- **WhatsApp (D75, F22 for WhatsApp).** The check stays in front of the gateway (D76), but its token is requested in the background when the card mounts, and again after each use. Cloudflare shows its challenge only when it asks the visitor to interact.
  - A press then waits for the gateway only, and opens `wa.me` within the click's activation (C: `rv37-31`, under 5 s).
  - If the activation has expired when the number arrives (`navigator.userActivation.isActive` is false), the button becomes an "Open WhatsApp" link for one more press, instead of failing silently. This fallback needs the owner's confirmation.
  - The server-side check is unchanged: one single-use token per gateway call, bound to the action and the hostname.
  - Whether `wa.me` opens the app directly or WhatsApp's own page with its open button is decided by the device and the browser, not by the site.
- **F23.** A Cloudflare error rejects `getToken()` at once, so the refusal toast comes without the 30 s wait. The console's error code for the owner's press of Call is still asked for.
- **Order.** Revision 34 (R115, R116) → Opus review → Revision 35 (D75, D76, F22, F23) → R78 (c) in Revision 36.

### 10. Owner decisions D77 and D78, and the console of the failed press of Call (Opus, 2026-10-23)

- **D77 (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** to Opus's proposal to check for a per-account limit on number reveals and to add one if there is none: `Yes, add it.` The owner did not name a number. Opus proposes at most 20 reveals per account per hour and 50 per 24 hours, with the same limits per IP. This needs the owner's confirmation.
  - Read-only check: `contactGateway.ts:22-27` lists four steps (shape, verified viewer, human check, database function) and no limit.
  - The v8a function text (`docs/sessions/evidence/task923/db-catalog/proposed-hardening-v8a.sql`) has no counting either.
  - The only existing pattern is the inquiry's limit: `submitListingInquiry.ts:35-51`, 5 per hour per IP and per sender, counted in the database, refusing when the count fails.
  - A gateway limit needs a record of every reveal. The gateway records a contact event for WhatsApp only (`contactGateway.ts:27`).
- **D78 (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** to the "Open WhatsApp" fallback for a slow network: `Yes, I agree. But the card should probably tell the user something like "Your network is very slow, press the button again", so that the user understands why WhatsApp did not open at once.`
  - The text and its four translations are Revision 35's. The cause can be the check as well as the network, so the wording must not blame only the network.
- **The console of the press of Call (owner's paste, 2026-10-23).** It has no Turnstile error code.
  - Two Cloudflare requests failed:
    - the Private Access Token request (`/pat/`), which Cloudflare's widget makes and tolerates;
    - a GET to `brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com`.
  - Read-only check from the owner's machine:
    - that host has no A record and resolves to IPv6 addresses only;
    - `curl -6` to `challenges.cloudflare.com` fails (exit 6), and `curl -4` answers 200.
  - So the machine has no IPv6 route, and that request is Cloudflare's IPv6 probe. It is not shown to be the cause.
  - The code is missing because the on-demand widget passes Turnstile an error callback, which receives the code, and `CaptchaWidget.tsx:108` drops it.
  - **F23 is therefore extended:** Revision 35 also records the Turnstile error code, without personal data, so that a failed check can be diagnosed. The cause of the owner's failed press stays open until then.

### 11. Owner decisions D77 (numbers), D78 (text) and D79; the desktop toast (Opus, 2026-10-23)

- **D77, numbers (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** `20 per hour, 60 per day.`
  - The per-IP limit is not the account limit. The owner asked whether an IP limit of 20 per hour and 60 per day would also cap a verified user, and it would.
  - Several people can share one IP: an office, a family, or a mobile operator's shared address.
  - Opus's proposal: 60 per hour and 200 per day per IP, above the verified limit of D79. This needs the owner's confirmation.
- **D79 (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** `We also have the verified user; we can give them a separate limit, for example 35 per 1 hour, 120 per day.`
  - Verified means `profiles.is_verified` (`src/types/database.ts:174`).
  - The gateway must read it from the profile of the viewer that step 2 verified, never from the request.
- **D78, text (owner, 2026-10-23):** the fallback text of §10 is confirmed: "Could not open WhatsApp at once — the connection was too slow. Press the button again." Revision 35 adds it in sq, en, uk and it.
- **The desktop toast (owner, 2026-10-23, translated):** `the error toast does not appear on desktop versions after pressing the buttons, but on mobile it appears.`
  - `rv37-32-toast-probe.txt` checked it on the owner's local server, signed in with HYDRATION_AGENT1, pressing Call without answering the challenge. Server Action POSTs were aborted, so nothing was written.
  - At 1440 px, 30.4 s after the press, the refusal toast is in the top-right container (rect 984,65,340×60; z-index 400; opacity 1). The element on top at its centre is the toast itself (`rv37-32-toast-1440.png`).
  - At 390 px it shows at 30.3 s, full width under the header.
  - So the toast is raised and visible on a desktop. Two causes fit the owner's observation:
    1. When the check passes, the gateway answers 200 (the owner's Network screenshot), and then the browser blocks the WhatsApp window or a desktop has no `tel:` handler. That path raises no toast at all (F22).
    2. On a desktop the toast appears in the far top-right corner, away from the pressed button, and closes after 4 s (`NOTIFICATION_AUTO_CLOSE = 4000`, `notificationVariants.ts:33`).
  - Revision 35 removes case 1: Show number shows the number in the card, and a blocked WhatsApp window shows D78's text in the card. It also states, for every refusal of the card's buttons, where its message appears.

### Deviations

1. **The Storybook build carries the real Turnstile site key.** `.env.local` is read at build time, so the production card of the `Default` Story loaded Cloudflare, and (with `prefetch`) executed it at load. A headless press of WhatsApp then shows no toast within the census's 8 s settle bound, and the state fails `portal-count` (`r35-07b2`, 32 jobs). I reproduced it with a Playwright probe against the first build (Cloudflare requests, no notification at 6.5 s). CI has no site key, and the widget then renders nothing and resolves `dev-noop-token`. So the evidence build was repeated with `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` set to empty for that one command (no file changed), and census and locale-leak ran on it. I cannot say whether this state passed on the first build before R117: no earlier evidence ran it since R113. **Opus: decide whether the registry row should survive a build that holds a site key.**
2. **`scripts/rendered-interaction-states.json`.** The row's click selector is positional. R118 (c) inserts two sections before the "production wiring" section, which moved from child 7 to child 9, so the first census run failed `open-failed` for 32 jobs (`r35-07b1`). I changed `7` to `9` in the row's two selectors. The file is in the D8_D9 scope. This is a change the kickoff did not list.
3. **`check:design-tokens` exits 1** on three findings in two files no Task 923 contract names (`Map.module.css`, `input-chrome.css`); the output equals `rv34-02`. I did not edit them.
4. **Path of the sheet test.** §59.2 names `src/components/auth/__tests__/AuthSheet.test.tsx`, which does not exist. The existing file is `src/modules/auth/components/__tests__/AuthSheet.test.tsx`.

### For Opus

- Keyboard focus: after Show number the first button is replaced by a link (a different DOM element), so the existing focus-return in `handleContactClick` finds `pressed` disconnected and focus ends on `body`. R119 (e) kept the focus return unchanged, so I did not change it.
- `getToken()` shares one promise between two concurrent calls (one pending request, as R117 (b) says). The container's guard already ignores a second press.
- After a timeout I clear the "execution running" flag, so the next request starts a new `execute()`. R117 does not say this; the alternative leaves the widget waiting forever when Cloudflare never answers.
- I ran no deliberate break of the new cases, no GR-12 parity census, and no GR-3j reflow probe beyond the rendered state census above; §59.2 lists none of them.

I logged the focus return temporarily and saw why: the animation frame fired 3 ms after it was registered, before React had committed the replacement link. ### Acceptance criteria

- **AC126, AC129.** The nine new cases pass (4 server unit, 4 integration, 1 frontend); both breaks fail their case on the intended assertion and the restored file has an equal sha256; the existing gateway and container cases pass (`r37-03a`, `r37-05`). Met.

The report ends with `PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED`. Met.

### Deviations

1. **The address parser treats an empty header as absent.** R126 (a) says "the first trimmed address of `x-forwarded-for`, or `x-real-ip`, or null". I wrote `...?.trim() || hdrs.get('x-real-ip')?.trim() || null`, so an empty or blank `x-forwarded-for` falls through to `x-real-ip` and then to the null bucket. With `??` (the message limit's form, C1142) an empty string would have been stored as the address `''`, a bucket of its own. The tests cover the trimmed first entry, `x-real-ip` alone, both headers, and neither. Opus: say if you want the `??` form.
2. **Pre-edit hashes.** I did not record a pre-edit sha256 of the other ten paths before editing them, because the working tree held earlier uncommitted work and I did not hash first. Only `ListingContact.tsx` has one, reconstructed as described above.
3. **The reveal double answers `users.is_verified` by its selected column.** The existing double answered every `users` read with the whole profile row. The gateway's flag read is `select('is_verified')`, so the double dispatches on that column string and answers only that column (R128 (c): "a missing `users` row" per test). Every other read is unchanged.
4. **Operations on the reveal record are tracked in `revealOps`, not `state.reads`.** The existing inquiry cases assert `state.reads` equals `['users']`; the reveal table is therefore kept out of that list. `revealOps` also records the verified-flag read, so a refusal that reads the flag would fail the existing deny cases.
5. **`SEC-X-INT-REVEAL-LIMIT` carries two controls beyond the written deny.** A viewer with 19 rows is served and gets one row (the allow control for the hour limit), and the viewer with 20 rows can still reveal a listing already among the 20 (the repeat at the limit, no new row).
6. **`SEC-X-INT-REVEAL-TABLE-DENY` uses its own synthetic person.** An earlier case of the file reveals through the gateway as the file's shared `viewer`, which now writes a reveal row; the deny case needs an exact row set, so it makes `reveal-table-deny`.
7. **`cli.mjs verify` exits 1** on the missing R43, R46 and R83 files, as expected (Review 34, N3).
8. **`check:design-tokens` exits 1**, as R130 (g) expects; its findings equal `rv39-09`.
9. **The first mobile receipt was refused** by the helper (see above); no write happened between the refusal and the corrected receipt.

### For Opus

- The count is a read followed by a later insert, so parallel requests can pass the limit by their number (the same open point as the message limit). The comment in `checkRevealLimit` says so. No concurrent-transaction case exists in this revision and none is required by §61.2.
- A refused reveal has already looked up the number (R126 places the limit after the lookup); the number is not returned, and `[SEC-X-SRV-REVEAL-LIMIT]` asserts the answer holds none.
- `is_verified` is read as `=== true`; any other value counts as a standard account (the column is never null, C1135).
- An automated security review flagged the address source (medium): the first entry of `x-forwarded-for` is client-controlled wherever the platform appends to the header instead of overwriting it, so the per-IP limit of D80 could be sidestepped by varying that entry. I kept it because R126 (a) names exactly this source (as in the message limit, C1142) and I may not change the design. The per-account limits of D77 and D79 do not depend on the address, so they stand either way. If the deployment platform overwrites the header, the finding does not apply. A change (the platform's own address header, or `net.isIP()` validation with an invalid value going to the null bucket) is an Opus decision for the message limit and the reveal limit together.

### 4. Finding F30 (P2, task design, Opus): the revealed number outlives a sign-out

- **The owner's question** (faithful translation): `If a user signed in, pressed "Show number", then signed out and signed in again, the number is visible. Is that correct UX from the point of view of data protection?`
- **The cause.** R119 kept the revealed number as component state "for the life of the page". The detail view renders the card with no key. On a listing page, the header's sign-out calls `router.refresh()`, which keeps a client component's state.
- **The proof.** Opus's probe `rv41-01-session-change.probe.test.tsx` (`rv41-01-probe.txt`, 1 passed) re-renders the real container as signed in, then as a guest, then as signed in again:
  - while signed out, the number is not in the page;
  - after the new sign-in, the number link is back with no new gateway call.
- **The answer to the owner: no, it is not correct.**
  - On a shared device, the next account signed in in that tab sees the previous account's numbers without the Cloudflare check, the limit or a reveal row.
  - One person's numbers stay in the page's memory after their sign-out.
- **The correction is R131.** The page keys the card by the viewer, so a sign-out or another account starts it empty. The same account's new press within 24 hours is free (D83).

- **AC136.** Both new self-test cases pass and the full verify run is green. The six Stories pass with the two exemptions counted in the two Login rows and nowhere else. The break fails and the restore is byte-equal. Met.

All assertions of `ProfileTab.deletePassword`, `ProfileTab.googleReauth` (including `SEC-927-FE-REAUTH-*`) and `emailChange.security.test.ts` pass, and none of those three files was edited. GR-12 census, GR-3j probes, zero-hit grep, `check-mobile-adaptation-contract`, `typecheck`, `lint` (0 errors), `build` and `build-storybook` exit 0. `check:ui-contract -- --base … --head HEAD` was **not** run: it reads committed revisions, and none of this work is committed. I ran `check:ui-contract:verify`, which validates the working-tree registry (see Not tested). Met, except that item.

### Deviations and assumptions

1. **`placeholder` on the e-mail field.** R83 (a) lists a label and a description for the `TextInput`. I also set `placeholder={t('email_change_hint')}` (the text of the description). The unchanged `ProfileTab.googleReauth.security.test.tsx` (outside this contract, so I could not edit it) finds the field with `getByPlaceholderText(t.email_change_hint)` in two places, and `deletePassword` does in two; without the placeholder SEC-927-FE-REAUTH-* fail. It is today's placeholder, so the field shows the hint twice while it is empty. Remove it only together with those test queries (a Task 927 change). Opus decides.
2. **The submit text.** The tests find the action by the name `common.save` ("Save"). I gave the new key `cabinet.email_change_submit` the same wording as `common.save` in each locale (Save / Ruaj / Зберегти / Salva), i.e. today's button text. The other three new texts are my wording and Opus may change them: `email_section_title` (Change email / Ndrysho emailin / Змінити email / Cambia email), `email_new_label` (New email / Email i ri / Новий email / Nuova email), `email_change_pending_title` (Confirm your new email / Konfirmoni emailin e ri / Підтвердіть новий email / Conferma la nuova email). The title is not the first words of the message ("Verification pending — …") on purpose.
3. **A refused resend.** R83 (a) puts the error alert inside the form only, so a refused resend (the limit of three an hour) would show nothing. Today's block shows it. The View also shows the red alert between the waiting notice and the resend action. The SEC-X cases do not cover it; the third test in `CabinetEmailChangeSection.security.test.tsx` does.
4. **`noValidate` on the form.** The browser's own bubble for `type="email"` would pre-empt the container's `EMAIL_RE` check and its localized `error_email_invalid`, which R83 (b) keeps. `Stack` types no `noValidate`, so it is passed through a module-level constant, the way the sibling passes `hintDescriptionProps`.
5. **No current e-mail, no field.** The View renders the detail field only when `currentEmail` is not empty (today's block did the same with `email &&`).
6. **Mantine's info `Alert` also has `role="alert"`**, so the new test file asserts the refusal by its text where the waiting notice is on screen.
7. **`r40-01`.** The earlier session's `r40-01-r136-blocked-scope.txt` and this session's `r40-01-census-verify.txt` share the number only.
8. The first run of my GR-3j probe flagged a 1 px rounding of `scrollHeight` on Mantine's hint, a latent `text-overflow: ellipsis` style on the Alert that clips nothing, and the 42 px inner `<input>` of the `PasswordInput` inside its 44 px wrapper. I corrected the probe to the census's own rules (a clipping box, an active ellipsis, the wrapper as the touch area). The product code was not changed for any of them. The 196 cells with a latent ellipsis style are Mantine's Alert (the sibling red Alert has the same); the census counts none of them.

## Owner's local AC12 of Task 927, part 2 (2026-10-24)

The owner's results (owner's words, translated):
- `accounts.google.com` blocked: "the red message appeared, I confirm."
- A Google-only account, more than 10 minutes after its sign-in: done.
- The e-mail change asks for Google, and the change continues: done.
- The owner's observation:
  - One browser had user 1 signed in on lero.al in one tab, and user 2, signed in with Google, on localhost in another.
  - The owner changed user 2's e-mail and pressed the confirmation link in Gmail.
  - The link opened lero.al, where user 1 was signed in, and lero.al showed the e-mail change page.
  - The owner asked whether every session in that browser should end, or whether this happened only because of lero.al and localhost.

**Opus's analysis.**

FACT:
- The link's base is `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? 'https://lero.al'` (`src/modules/cabinet/actions/index.ts:641-643`), and `.env.local` sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://lero.al`. So a change started on localhost mails a lero.al link.
- localhost and lero.al use the same Supabase project. The project ref in production's public bundle equals the one in `.env.local`, compared without printing it. This is owner D67, "One project before launch" in `security-test-environment.md`. So lero.al consumed the token of user 2's change.
- The public confirm-email page calls `consumeEmailChangeToken` (`index.ts:741-815`). The token alone identifies the account, through the service-role client. The browser's session is neither read nor changed.
- After the change, `end_user_sessions` ends every session of the token's account, user 2 (`index.ts:796-805`).

INFERENCE: this is correct behaviour, not a defect:
- User 1's session is not user 2's, and the token gives no right over it.
- If opening a link ended the viewer's own session, anyone could sign anyone out by sending them a link.
- The cookies of localhost and lero.al are separate anyway.
- The two-site situation comes only from local testing against the shared project. In production the link and the change are on the same site.

UNVERIFIED, asked of the owner:
- the confirm page showed success (the green check);
- after a reload, localhost no longer has user 2 signed in.

AC12 stays open for those two answers and for the deletion check.

  - Mantine 8.3.18's own `.mantine-Alert-message` sets `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` (`node_modules/@mantine/core/styles/Alert.css:56-60`). The message wraps (`white-space: normal`), so this style clips nothing. The executor's diagnosis `r42-03b` measured 0 clipped in 68 cells.

### What the code does now

- **`deleteAccount(userId, { reason })` (R141).** It reads the Cloudinary id of every file first: the avatar and profile logo, every image of the person's listings, the logo of each company with `created_by` = the person, and each verification document; a failed read answers `delete_failed` with nothing deleted. Then `auth.admin.deleteUser` (one transaction). Then `deleteAsset` per unique id and one `remove` of the `avatars` objects under `<userId>/`. A thrown call or a `reference lookup failed` answer counts in `filesNotRemoved`. Logs carry `userId`, `reason`, ids and codes only.
- **Callers (R142).** `hardDeleteUser` keeps permission, session, own-id refusal and `rankCheck`, then `deleteAccount(…, { reason: 'staff' })`. `deleteOwnAccount` keeps session and re-authentication, then `deleteAccount(…, { reason: 'self' })`. The archive step, the profile delete and the `profile_deleted_auth_failed` branch are gone; `softDeleteUser` and its test rows are gone; `ProfileTab` shows `error_deleting` for any other failure.
- **Texts (R143) and the typed word (R144).** The four locales carry the texts of R43 (e) word for word; the archive point and the two obsolete keys are removed; the admin delete dialog passes `typedConfirm={{ word: DELETE_CONFIRM_WORD, label: t('dialogs.delete_type_confirm') }}` and nothing else.
- **R145.** The `listing_images.public_id` read is removed from the reference check (seven reads stay, an error still keeps the file); the two security tests lose it; Task 144's unit test file is deleted; SEC-DEL-INT-ALLOW now asserts one `[deleteAsset]` entry with `outcome: 'DRY_RUN'` and no `lookup` for each of the four Cloudinary ids; the stale comment of `hardDeleteUser` is corrected (comment only).

1. **Runners.** The transcripts were written by `run.mjs`, `run-sh.mjs` (the same with a shell) and `run-int44.mjs` (it derives `SECURITY_TEST_PROJECT_REF` from the host of `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` without printing it, as in C799), all in the session scratchpad. `r44-00` and `r45-00` ran as one `bash -c` script whose text is the `command:` line. The first `r44-01` attempt wrote an empty transcript (`spawnSync` could not start `npx` without a shell); it was rewritten by `run-sh.mjs`.
2. **The third new file of r44-01.** `deleteAccount.integration.test.ts` is excluded from the default run by `vitest.config.ts`, so r44-01 holds two new files; the third runs in r44-02 (`r44-01b` shows the exclusion).
3. **Extra transcripts.** `r44-01b`, `r44-02b`, `r44-02c` (the read-only probe that found F15), `r44-04a`, `r45-01b`, `r45-02b`; the run before R145 is kept under `r44-06*-pre-r145-*`.
4. **Hook refusals, nothing written.** Bash commands that named the kickoff path together with a heredoc or a `>` in a title text were refused by the kickoff write hook; a `node -e` text that named `messages/it.json` was read as a write to `messages/it.js` and refused. I removed the angle brackets from the title and used plain edits. No kickoff receipt was registered and the kickoff is not edited.
5. **Shell state.** Several shell calls moved the tool's working directory into `docs/sessions/evidence/task923/`; every later command begins with an explicit `cd` to the root, and the transcripts record the root as cwd.
6. **Fixture choices of the real-boundary suite.** The click of SEC-DEL-INT-ALLOW uses the channel `whatsapp`, the only one the application writes (`ListingContactChannel`), not "phone". `listing_images` accepts only addresses of the project's own Cloudinary cloud (`listing_images_url_prefix_check`), so the test reads that public prefix from one existing row (read only) and builds synthetic ids after it; the whole run is `CLOUDINARY_DELETE_MODE=dry-run`. The synthetic `text/plain` object was accepted by the `avatars` bucket.
7. **SEC-DEL-INT-DENY did not exercise the rank rule.** In the real project the moderator role does not hold `users.hard_delete` (`r44-02` prints `the moderator role holds users.hard_delete: false`), so the permission refused. The rank rule is proved by the unit case SEC-DEL-SRV-DENY ("a moderator deleting an administrator") and by break B3. "A blocked administrator" in SEC-DEL-SRV-DENY is modelled by the permission double answering false, because `@/lib/auth/permissions` is a double by the task's own list.
8. **More than the minimum in existing tests.** Besides the changes the task names, I added a few cases where a removed behavior left a gap: `hardDeleteUser.smoke` (own id, rank refusal, `filesNotRemoved` still `{}`), `deleteOwnAccount.smoke` (`filesNotRemoved`, no password), `cabinetFailures` ("a file that could not be removed", "no listings"), and I put `hardDeleteUser` into the allowed rows of `userAdministration` in place of the removed `softDeleteUser` row. `adminActorRank`'s control now uses `hardDeleteUser` for both actors.
9. **After-edit hashes of `r44-03` and the comment edit of R145 (f).** `r44-03` restored `src/modules/admin/actions/index.ts` to `16324650…6c30`, its hash at that time. R145 (f) then changed one comment line, so the final hash is `96b60f89…2bec1`. `r44-02` and `r44-03` also ran on the integration test file before R145 (e); `r45-02` and `r45-03` are the runs on its final form, and `r44-01` was rerun on the final unit files.
10. **Assertion order and a locator.** In SEC-DEL-SRV-ALLOW the check of the released ids precedes the check of the read order, so break B2 fails on the missing id as the AC says; in SEC-DEL-FE-ADMIN the field is found with `queryByLabelText` and asserted non-null, so break B4 fails on an assertion and not on a locator error.

No file written by me contains Russian: the transcripts, scripts, code, comments and test names are English, and the only non-English text is locale data (`messages/*.json` and the expected texts of `adminDeleteDialog.security.test.tsx`).

### What the code does now

- **R146 (a).** The `listings` read is gone. The images are read once, through their listing: `db.from('listing_images').select('url, listings!inner(user_id)').eq('listings.user_id', userId)`.
- **R146 (b).** `collectPublicIds` reads `users`, `listing_images`, `companies` and `verification_requests` through one helper. Each page is `.order('id').range(from, from + 999)` (`PAGE_SIZE = 1000`); `from` starts at 0 and grows by the rows the page returned; the read stops at the first page with no row; an error on any page returns the same `{ ok: false, source, code }` as before, so the deletion is refused with no Auth deletion and no release.
- **R146 (c).** The order (collect, Auth deletion, files), the release, the Storage step and the logs are untouched. Only the doc comment of step 1 gains "page by page so that no row is left out".
- **R146 (d), the test.** The double gains `order` (logged `order:<table>:<column>`) and `range(from, to)` (logged `range:<table>:<from>-<to>`; it answers that slice of the table's rows), and `world.failPage` (`<table>:<from>`) to fail one page.
  - SEC-DEL-SRV-ALLOW: the four `eq:` entries are `users:id`, `listing_images:listings.user_id`, `companies:created_by` and `verification_requests:user_id`; the image select is `url, listings!inner(user_id)`; no `from:listings` and no `in:` entry; every table is ordered by `id`. The new part has 2 345 image rows with distinct ids: the image read asks `range:listing_images:0-999`, `1000-1999`, `2000-2999` and `2345-3344`, and each id is released once (2 349 ids in all).
  - SEC-DEL-SRV-ERR: the failing reads are the four of (b); a new part fails the second page of 1 500 images (`listing_images:1000`): `delete_failed`, no Auth deletion, no release, the log line carries `source: 'listing_images'` and code `XX000`.

A signed-in person who opens `/auth/register` in a new tab on `localhost` stays on the loader; before R147 they reached the cabinet. The sign-in page itself never gives a signed-in first state on a full load, because the server redirects first.

### What the code does now

- **R148 (a).** `AuthController.mount()`, after it subscribes to the Supabase events and the visibility listener, calls `syncFromServer()` once when the status is `refreshing` and `this.inflight === null`. The comment says why: React Strict Mode mounts, cleans up and mounts again in development, and the cleanup aborts the re-check in flight. A first mount from the constructor's state does nothing new. Nothing else in the controller changed.
- **R148 (b).** `AuthRedirect.tsx`: only the header comment changed. It now says the sign-in page renders the bridge only when SSR found no signed-in viewer, the sign-up page renders it with no server check, and an `authenticated` status at mount is re-checked once. No code, no markup change.
- **R148 (c), the test.** A `browserFetch` double replaces the fetch double: an aborted request rejects with an error named `AbortError`, and a request resolves (after a macrotask) only if it was not aborted. SEC-D29-FE-STALE-DENY and SEC-D29-FE-STALE-ALLOW each gain (iii): the tree under `React.StrictMode` at its root, a full load with a signed-in first user. DENY (iii), answer `{ user: null }`: no `router.replace`, the sheet opens once, the session-lost mark is stored, `signOut('local')` is called, the status is `unauthenticated`. ALLOW (iii), answer an active user: `router.replace('/en/cabinet')` once, the sheet does not open, `signOut` is not called, the status is `authenticated`. (i) and (ii) of both cases keep their assertions and pass with the new double. Each case stays one `it` with its exact contract name.
- **R148 (d).** Nothing else changed.

### What the code does now

- **R149 (a).** In `AdminUserProfilePage` the account lookup ends with `.maybeSingle()` instead of `.single()`. An absent account answers no row and no error, so the page redirects to `/admin/users?notice=user_gone` without the `console.error` line. The `console.error` line, both redirects and everything else are as they were. `generateMetadata` is unchanged (it still reads with `.single()` and logs nothing).
- **R149 (b), the double.** `state` holds `row` (or null) and `failure` (or null) instead of one answer. `single()` answers the failure if one is set, else the row, else `{ data: null, error: PGRST116 }` with code `PGRST116`, details `The result contains 0 rows`, hint null and message `Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object`. `maybeSingle()` answers the failure if one is set, else the row or null with no error. The `users` chain supports `select`, `eq`, `single` and `maybeSingle`; any other call still throws, and so does awaiting the chain without a terminal call.
- **R149 (b), the cases.** SEC-X-SRV-ADMIN-USER-GONE also asserts `expect(console.error, 'an absent account is not a failed query').not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. SEC-X-SRV-ADMIN-USER-QUERY-ERROR sets a failure `{ message: 'down' }` and asserts, with the message `a failed lookup is still logged`, that `console.error` was called once and with `'AdminUserProfilePage: user query failed'` and an object containing that failure and the id. DELETED and PRESENT keep their assertions. The `console.error` spy of `beforeEach` stays. Each case stays one `it` with its contract name.
- **R149 (c).** Nothing else changed.
